_comment: Reasoned statuses for failure-matrix cases that cannot be executed as live or automated tests yet. Used by scripts/matrix-coverage.py only when no test/lab evidence exists, or, for an entry with 'requires' (evidence kinds such as native_e2e), until evidence of one of those kinds exists; the reason is shown as the case's note either way. 'blocked', 'partial' and 'not_applicable' are never counted as passed; 'verified_check' records an executed check script (exact command, artifacts and result) that CI re-runs on every release run: either on each built artifact (REL-002) or on a pinned input that describes a release (the website commit, REL-006/007/008). Its reason says what the check covers and whether it gates the release. An entry with "pinned": true is never promoted by discovered tests or lab passes that name the case (its evidence is elsewhere, such as a hosted workflow run); only editing the entry changes that. A failing lab result still shows as failing_live.

TRUST-012.reason: Anvil does not ingest or correlate gateway logs; it never confirms anything from temporal proximity. Operator logs are used only as lab ground truth.

LOAD-012.reason: The optional JMeter adapter is not built in this release (plan 14.3: only after native load works). Native load covers the required workloads; see docs/load.md.

PROTO-004.reason: HTTP/2 GOAWAY and REFUSED_STREAM are typed (exchange.h2_goaway / exchange.h2_refused_stream, dispatch derived from REFUSED_STREAM) but a live multi-stream graceful-shutdown fixture is not built yet.

REL-001.reason: Hosted release smoke (.github/workflows/release-smoke.yml) against the published, unsigned anvil-v0.1.5 assets (each checked against SHA256SUMS): run 41275148483 on PR head 70dde1b2, with the same per-target result as the earlier runs 41273823587 (head f00000e6), 41270507104 (head 4d707c55), 41255989645 (head 8edbdfa8), 41254710916 (head 51fbc0b8), 41189324002 (head adb4d3f) and 41185287833 (head 7f17212). This evidence comes from pull_request-triggered runs against the published assets; once the workflow is on main, the run that publishing a release starts (release: published) is the routine check. For each target, the smoke installs the package natively on a fresh runner and launches the installed app (window observed, and a webview content process attributed to the app: on Linux by process tree, on macOS by launchctl's responsible pid, on Windows as a WebView2 descendant). It then imports samples/workspaces/anvil-samples.anvil, sends its Healthy/OK request to a loopback listener (HTTP 200) and relaunches the app; a target stops at its first failed step. Six targets pass every step: macOS arm64 DMG (macos-15), macOS x86_64 DMG (native Intel macos-15-intel), Windows x64 NSIS and MSI (windows-2025), Linux x64 .deb (Ubuntu 26.04) and .rpm (Fedora 44). The x64 AppImage fails at its first launch (a package failure): the app starts and shows its window, but its WebKit web process aborts with EGL_BAD_PARAMETER, so it never reached the import, the call or the relaunch. The fix, ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#463, is merged but not released: 0.1.5's AppImage stays broken until the next release ships a rebuilt one. The GUI was not driven: the import and the call go through the release CLI archive on the app's data directory. Recorded bypasses: Gatekeeper and SmartScreen were never consulted (the assets carried no quarantine attribute or Mark-of-the-Web); the DMG license was accepted non-interactively; the installers ran silently, the MSI as an administrator without a UAC prompt; local .deb/.rpm packages and the AppImage ran without a package-signature check. Still blocked: signed and notarized first-run acceptance on macOS and Windows (Gatekeeper, SmartScreen, Keychain), which needs owner credentials (ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2). Linux has no platform code signing, so it waits on no credentials.

REL-003.reason: Refusal is automated against built bundles: .github/workflows/updater-e2e.yml builds the e2e-instrumented desktop bundle (AppImage on ubuntu-26.04, .app on macos-15) with a minisign key generated for the run and a loopback update endpoint (requireSignedVersion stays on), and drives the app's update_install command through WebDriver (apps/desktop/e2e/updater/). An update signed by another key, one with a corrupted signature and one altered after signing are each refused with the plugin's minisign error after the app requested the manifest and the artifact; during each refusal the bundle's files (SHA-256, mode, size, inode, mtime), the reported version and the persistent profile files (SQLite's -shm read index excluded) are unchanged. Relaunched afterwards, the bundle matches its recorded contents and reports its own version, and the same profile unlocks with the same workspaces; a validly signed update installs and the relaunched bundle reports the new version. The rel_003_* unit tests run more signature variants through the same updater path on Tauri's mock runtime. Not covered: Windows (MSI/NSIS), release-profile bundles without the e2e feature, TLS and the published latest.json, .deb/.rpm (no in-app update). The valid path was also run by hand on macOS arm64 from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 (release runs 36827029766 and 36835226571, updater key BFE08514FEC0E65A); macOS may re-prompt for Keychain access after an update of an unsigned build (ferrum-edge/ferrum-anvil#2).

REL-006.reason: Executed check: the hosted website check recorded in docs/verification/website-evidence.md (pinned ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit 1f89dfd94915aa419b80decf9666dc1bcc769df8, command, Node version, runs and counts; workflow_dispatch run 41359301938 passes 459 of 461 tests with 0 failed and 2 unrelated live CDN checks skipped). release.yml calls it on every release run, beside the build; it does not gate the draft release. It covers the website at the pinned commit, which describes anvil-v0.1.5; a later release's pages are covered once the pin moves. Tests (tests/anvil.test.js, 'Anvil downloads match the release evidence'): each download.html row's OS and architecture, and each link's package label and column, match the linked asset name (architecture aliases mapped; a swapped architecture, OS, package or column is rejected by a negative test); every displayed download is that platform's installer or CLI archive in the recorded release-evidence.json, and the table shows each of them once; the recorded SHA256SUMS lines hash to GitHub's digest of the published SHA256SUMS asset, each of the 33 listed assets has a recorded digest equal to its SHA256SUMS entry (only SHA256SUMS and release-evidence.json are unlisted), and every displayed download is checksummed there. 'published preview links and bounded claims' requires every release-download link in Anvil content to be a published asset of the audited tag, so no asset name is inferred from the tag; tests/releases.test.js requires download.html to link SHA256SUMS and release-evidence.json. The site displays no hashes and points to SHA256SUMS. Scope: asset names and digests are compared as recorded in tests/fixtures/release-audit.json (GitHub release API, checked 2026-10-31), not re-fetched on each run; the release API returned the same 35 asset names and digests on 2026-11-01.

REL-007.reason: Executed check: the hosted website check recorded in docs/verification/website-evidence.md (pinned ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit 1f89dfd94915aa419b80decf9666dc1bcc769df8, command, Node version, runs and counts; workflow_dispatch run 41359301938 passes 459 of 461 tests with 0 failed and 2 unrelated live CDN checks skipped). release.yml calls it on every release run, beside the build; it does not gate the draft release. It covers the website at the pinned commit, which describes anvil-v0.1.5; a later release's pages are covered once the pin moves. Tests: tests/components.test.js 'Anvil navigation entries' runs the site's components.js, with its real DOMContentLoaded handler, for root (/, /index.html), extensionless and .html (/anvil, /anvil.html, /foundry), guide (/guides/, /guides/anvil-getting-started, /guides/anvil-diagnostics.html) and other nested (/install/linux, /plugins/) page paths: the desktop Tools dropdown, the mobile menu and the footer each carry one Anvil link labelled unsigned preview, written with ./ or ../ as the page's depth requires and resolving to /anvil, and the footer's Anvil guides link resolves to /guides/#anvil-guides; on /anvil and /anvil.html Tools is the only active section and the desktop and mobile Anvil links carry aria-current="page"; an Anvil guide activates Docs and marks no Anvil link current; another Tools page does not mark Anvil current; no injected link uses .html. 'normalizePath' and 'resolveActiveNav' cover the same paths with and without .html, index and trailing slashes; 'the injected nav and banner use data hooks the listener handles' requires aria-controls on every dropdown toggle. tests/anvil.test.js checks that every local link in Anvil content (the six Anvil pages and the Anvil blocks on download, guides/index, index and releases) is extensionless and resolves from its own page, with its anchor; that the anchors other pages link to and the anvil.html jump links exist; that Anvil screenshots and brand images carry alt text; and that no link nests inside another on any page with a checked Anvil region. Scope: the shell is rendered in a Node vm with a minimal DOM, not a browser or a mobile viewport (the mobile menu is checked as markup); accessibility is the targeted aria-current, aria-controls and alt-text checks, not a full audit. No test asserts that a page mounts the shared nav; at the pinned commit 1f89dfd all ten of those pages carry nav-container and footer-container and load components.js at their depth.

REL-008.reason: Executed check: the hosted website check recorded in docs/verification/website-evidence.md (pinned ferrum-edge/ferrumedge commit 1f89dfd94915aa419b80decf9666dc1bcc769df8, command, Node version, runs and counts; workflow_dispatch run 41359301938 passes 459 of 461 tests with 0 failed and 2 unrelated live CDN checks skipped). release.yml calls it on every release run, beside the build; it does not gate the draft release. It covers the website at the pinned commit, which describes anvil-v0.1.5; a later release's pages are covered once the pin moves. Tests: tests/anvil-capabilities.test.js reads every claim element in the <main> and <head> of anvil.html and the five Anvil guides and in the Anvil blocks of index, guides/index, releases and download (824 elements, per `node tests/anvil-claims.js --counts` at that commit: paragraphs, list items, table cells, headings, labels, links, image alt text, page titles and descriptions; any other visible text there fails). The download table on download.html is the one table left out of the claim check; tests/releases.test.js and the REL-006 download tests cover it. Each element names the capabilities it claims in data-anvil-claim, and each capability must be backed in tests/fixtures/anvil-capabilities.json, recorded from ferrum-anvil at anvil-v0.1.5 (695308f2): a verified matrix case, the catalog outcome counts and public tokens, named tests with a line quoted from inside each test, or a doc or code quote. Every version, count, algorithm, format or product name in a clause must be a recorded value of a capability named there; every lowercase word and inline-code word must be in a reviewed list. Built-but-untested variants must carry their qualifier, and each behavior a test-backed claim asserts must be an audited behavior (a quoted test line or a verified case) or an untested behavior that is qualified in the copy, backed by another declared capability or stated as a limit. A negated audited phrase fails with its negation removed. Refused or unbuilt capabilities may appear only in limiting words; support-matrix cells must agree with each capability's support level. Claims resting on tests outside the verification matrix, or on code the claim says is untested, carry the dagger the #evidence-levels note explains. Screenshot alt text is bound to the e2e spec that captures the screen and the renderer files that draw it. tests/anvil.test.js 'published preview links and bounded claims' rejects exact or guaranteed root-cause claims and 'available now' wording in all Anvil content (must_not). Scope: the claims are compared with the recorded fixture; the website repository's own CI re-verifies that fixture against a checkout of anvil-v0.1.5, which this check does not repeat. Screenshot pixels are not compared with the current app. The check is word-level; its residual limits are listed in ferrumedge's README ('Residual limits of a word-level check'): a universal quantifier or paraphrase for a capability without tests is not audited, the relevance of a case, fact or backing-key quote is recorded for review rather than checked, markup that hides text is refused only from a fixed list, and text inserted by script at run time is not read.

REL-002.reason: 2026-09-25, macOS arm64, commit cf3a61c: `npx tauri build --ci --bundles app,dmg` and `cargo build --release --locked -p anvil-cli`, then `scripts/release-check.sh --runtime-probe --probe-seconds 15` over the .app, the .dmg, the raw anvil-desktop binary and the anvil CLI → pass (graph: no tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver / e2e feature; 0 of 11 hook strings; runtime probe: no WebDriver listener on TAURI_WEBDRIVER_PORT, no env-driven profile unlock). Negative control: the e2e debug build fails with all 11 strings. The release workflow runs the same check on every installer and archive.

UP-017.reason: Live reproduction blocked: Ferrum Edge 0.9.5 assigns port_exhaustion only to EADDRNOTAVAIL at connect (src/retry.rs) and the release binary has no lab dial-admission hook, while draining the lab host's real ephemeral ports would be unsafe. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_017_port_exhaustion_signal_is_coarse_and_hook_free (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the catalog's shared 502 connection_failure 'Backend unavailable' signal keeps the connection-failure family ambiguous, names port exhaustion only as an unknown-confidence candidate, never states port exhaustion or host resources at likely or above, and makes no TLS/DNS claim. It is neither a live nor a hook-based test.

UP-019.reason: Live reproduction blocked: upstream.trust_withdrawn is mesh-only in 0.9.5 and 0.9.7 (an accepted gateway trust publication withdraws an authority while an HBONE / sidecar-mTLS transport is established or reused). The mesh lab profile runs HBONE with SPIFFE identities and reproduces the unauthenticated-peer refusal, but it has no control plane publishing trust, so no withdrawal on a live tunnel is reproduced. Covered instead by the public-signal contract test up_019_trust_withdrawn_signal_makes_no_certificate_claim (crates/anvil-diagnostics/tests/upstream_setup_contract.rs): the shared 502 connection_failure signal stays ambiguous, lists trust withdrawal only as an unknown-confidence candidate, and yields no confirmed or likely certificate/TLS claim and no blame on the caller's certificate.
